interviewBank.q: When do you use a class instead of an id?
interviewBank.answer: Classes are reusable and are the default styling hook. An id is unique, so it is reserved for fragment targets, label associations and one-off references, not for styles that repeat.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a space and a child combinator?
interviewBank.answer: A space matches any descendant at any depth; > matches only elements whose direct parent is the one named. The child combinator is stricter and usually safer.

interviewBank.q: How specific is an attribute selector compared with a class?
interviewBank.answer: An attribute selector and a class selector both count as one class-level component. Specificity is equal, so source order decides between them.

defenseBank.q: A learner styles with ids everywhere.
defenseBank.answer: Ids cannot repeat and their specificity is hard to override, so the first variation forces a new id. Classes express reusable patterns and stay manageable.

defenseBank.q: Why not select by tag alone?
defenseBank.answer: A tag selector hits every instance on the page, including ones that need a different treatment. A class scopes the intent to the elements that share it.

interviewBank.q: Hex or HSL — which do you choose and why?
interviewBank.answer: Hex is compact and familiar for fixed brand values. HSL is easier to reason about when deriving variants, because hue, saturation and lightness are separate numbers.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between background and background-color?
interviewBank.answer: background is a shorthand that resets every background property; background-color sets only the colour. Using the shorthand after a colour can wipe the earlier layer.

interviewBank.q: How do you keep text readable on a gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Check contrast against the darkest and lightest part of the gradient, add a solid overlay behind the text, and never assume the middle of a gradient is the worst case.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks colours by eye only.

defenseBank.q: Why set a fallback background colour with an image?

interviewBank.q: rem or em — when do you use each?
interviewBank.answer: rem for anything that should follow the root scale: type, spacing, radii. em when a component should scale relative to its own font size, such as padding on a button.

interviewBank.q: Why can 100vw cause a horizontal scrollbar?
interviewBank.answer: On desktop vw includes the vertical scrollbar width, while the content area does not. 100% follows the containing block and avoids the mismatch.
clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value, but never below the minimum or above the maximum. It is the standard way to make type fluid without media queries.

defenseBank.q: A design uses px for every font size.
defenseBank.answer: px ignores the user’s font-size preference, which breaks zoom and accessibility. rem follows the root size and respects that setting.
steps: Change the browser default font size.
Switch to rem and show it scale.

defenseBank.q: Why is a unitless line-height safer?
defenseBank.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element’s own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio. A px line-height stays fixed and can overlap when the font grows.
steps: Show a large heading with 20px line-height.

interviewBank.q: Why does font-family take a list?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses the first family it can actually render. The list ends with a generic family so the page never falls back to an unrelated default.
A unitless number multiplies the element’s own font size, so it scales with nested text instead of staying a fixed length.

interviewBank.q: What is FOUT and how do you reduce it?
interviewBank.answer: Flash of unstyled text: fallback text is shown before the web font loads, then swaps. Preloading the font, using font-display and choosing a close fallback reduce the visible shift.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets body text to 12px to fit more.
defenseBank.answer: Small text costs readability and fails accessibility expectations. A 16px base with a wider measure and tighter spacing fits content without shrinking it.
Long lines make the eye lose its place on the return sweep; very short lines break rhythm. A 60–75 character measure is the readable range.

mcqBank.q: Which is a generic font family?
mcqBank.why: Generic families are the guaranteed fallbacks.
